edit.description: the cursor probe reads absence off the exit status git spells it with, and every other failure travels out as the header already claims
the unreadable-tree refusal, beside the unresolved-cursor arm it is currently indistinguishable from

summary: `resolvesInTree`'s bare catch folds an unreadable tree into `no such commit`, so a plan tick is told to rewrite a cursor that was correct
acceptance: only the exit status git spells a non-resolving ref with reads as absent; every other failure reaches the window's own bound and refuses as unreadable carrying git's text, so no refusal asks a tick to repair a cursor over a tree nothing could read
tests: a plan window over a tree git cannot read refuses as unreadable rather than as a cursor to repair
notes: Verified: `harness/gitRange.ts:104` catches everything, against the module header's own claim at `:19` that only a non-resolving cursor is a verdict. Measured — a bad ref exits 1 with empty stderr, a non-repository exits 128 saying so: git tells them apart, the shape `isAncestor` (`src/git.ts:227`) already keys on. `cursorWindow.ts:62` then renders the repair-your-cursor refusal in place of `bounded`'s (`:157`). `init.ts:424`'s unborn-HEAD read is unaffected — unborn HEAD exits 1, measured.
